headline: 153-run lead for Bangladesh as Tanzid Hasan Tamim hits maiden Test ton in Darwin
summary: Tanzid becomes the first Bangladeshi batter to score a Test century on Australian soil, helping the Tigers secure a dominant position on Day 2.
details: Bangladesh ended Day 2 of the first Test against Australia with a commanding 153-run lead, finishing at 351 for six. The Tigers' dominant position was anchored by a historic performance from opener Tanzid Hasan Tamim.

Tanzid struck a maiden Test century, scoring 101 off 197 balls. He became the first Bangladeshi batter ever to score a Test hundred on Australian soil and the second Bangladeshi to score a Test ton against Australia.
Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto also contributed significantly with 84 runs, while Mushfiqur Rahim added 36. The pair shared a 66-run partnership for the fourth wicket to further extend the lead.

Australia fought back in the post-tea session with three quick wickets. Josh Hazlewood dismissed Shanto, and Mitchell Starc removed Litton Das for a duck before Pat Cummins took the wicket of Mushfiqur Rahim.
Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32*) and Hasan Mahmud (13*) remained unbeaten at the end of the day, sharing an unbroken 43-run partnership to salvage a tricky period after the second new ball.
Bangladesh will look to build on their substantial lead on Saturday as the match continues at Marrara Stadium in Darwin.
caption:
History made in Darwin! 🇧🇩

Tanzid Hasan Tamim becomes the first Bangladeshi to score a Test century on Australian soil.

Bangladesh ended Day 2 of the first Test against Australia with a commanding 153-run lead, finishing at 351 for six. The Tigers' dominant position was anchored by a historic performance from opener Tanzid Hasan Tamim.

Tanzid struck a maiden Test century, scoring 101 off 197 balls. He became the first Bangladeshi batter ever to score a Test hundred on Australian soil and the second Bangladeshi to score a Test ton against Australia.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto also contributed significantly with 84 runs, while Mushfiqur Rahim added 36. The pair shared a 66-run partnership for the fourth wicket to further extend the lead.

Australia fought back in the post-tea session with three quick wickets. Josh Hazlewood dismissed Shanto, and Mitchell Starc removed Litton Das for a duck before Pat Cummins took the wicket of Mushfiqur Rahim.

Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32*) and Hasan Mahmud (13*) remained unbeaten at the end of the day, sharing an unbroken 43-run partnership to salvage a tricky period after the second new ball.

Bangladesh will look to build on their substantial lead on Saturday as the match continues at Marrara Stadium in Darwin.

headline: 8 workers die from toxic gas leak at Sitakunda shipyard
summary: The death toll rose to eight after workers inhaled toxic fumes while dismantling a ship without proper safety measures in Chattogram.
details: At least eight workers have died after inhaling toxic gas while dismantling a ship at a shipyard in Sitakunda, Chattogram.
The victims were working inside the vessel when they were exposed to lethal fumes, leading to their collapse and subsequent deaths.
Initial reports indicated five deaths, but the toll rose to eight as more workers succumbed to the poisoning.
Witnesses and reports suggest the work was being carried out without adequate safety equipment or precautions.
Several other workers were injured and rushed to the hospital for emergency treatment.
Local authorities and emergency services responded to the scene to recover the bodies and assist the injured.
caption:
8 workers dead. A routine job at a Sitakunda shipyard turned lethal when toxic gas filled the vessel.

At least eight workers have died after inhaling toxic gas while dismantling a ship at a shipyard in Sitakunda, Chattogram.

The victims were working inside the vessel when they were exposed to lethal fumes, leading to their collapse and subsequent deaths.

Initial reports indicated five deaths, but the toll rose to eight as more workers succumbed to the poisoning.

Witnesses and reports suggest the work was being carried out without adequate safety equipment or precautions.

Several other workers were injured and rushed to the hospital for emergency treatment.

Local authorities and emergency services responded to the scene to recover the bodies and assist the injured.
